newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO police ready to take over Hebron from Israelis.
newsitem.headline: PLO police ready to take over Hebron from Israelis.

text.p: As soon as Israeli soldiers lower their flag over Hebron, 400 PLO policemen will take charge of the volatile West Bank city.

Brigadier-General Abdel-Fattah al-Jaidi, commander of Palestinian security forces in the Hebron district, said 200 police and 200 members of the paramilitary National Security Forces were waiting at bases in the village of Dhahiriyeh and the town of Jericho for orders to move to Hebron.
The force will shoulder the daunting task of maintaining security in Hebron, a hotbed of Jewish and Islamic militancy where tensions can quickly flare into violence.
"As soon as the (Israeli) redeployment begins, our forces are ready to enter the city," Jaidi told Reuters.

Palestinians say the PLO has discreetly moved equipment and vehicles into Hebron over the past few months. Locally-recruited policemen are also ready to don uniforms and move as soon as orders are issued.

Under the Hebron accord, Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority may deploy up to 400 policemen in the 80 percent of Hebron that Israel will hand over to Palestinian rule, probably by the end of this week.
Some 20,000 Palestinians will remain under Israeli rule in the part of the city where about 400 Jewish settlers live or study.

Unlike the forces that took over six West Bank cities in 1995 under the West Bank self-rule deal, Palestinian police will have a difficult task keeping order in a city where Arab and Jew will continue to rub shoulders along an invisible line between the two parts of the city.
Armed Jewish settlers strongly opposed to the Hebron handover will be living just across the street from Palestinians under self-rule.

A settler from nearby Kiryat Arba massacred 29 Palestinians kneeling in prayer at Hebron's al-Ibrahimi mosque in 1994. On New Years day this year an Israeli soldier shot and wounded seven Palestinians in the market an attempt to thwart a Hebron deal.

Palestinian security forces will have 20 vehicles and will be armed with 100 rifles and 200 pistols. Apart from regular police duties, Palestinian security forces are expected to try to thwart possible guerrilla attacks against Israelis from the area under their control.
The agreement provides for joint patrols by Israeli and Palestinian forces. The PLO police will carry semi-automatic Ingram guns while the Israelis will be armed with M-16 automatic rifles.
Jaidi says the Palestinian police realise the task in Hebron, a city sacred to Jews and Moslems, will be more difficult than in the West Bank centres handed over in 1995.
"We are taking everything into consideration. But we are confident that with coordination with the Israeli side, this redeployment will go smoothly," Jaidi said.
